\section{f095 Follow-up: Capacity, Symmetry, and Decomposition}
\label{sec:f095}
All cells are dev-bank E quartets ($n{=}237$, seeds s11/s23/s47) unless noted; checkpoints, banks, and manifests are in \texttt{artifacts/f095\_campaign/}.
\paragraph{Three-part decomposition.} With per-quartet scores for states A/B/AB, $1-J$ splits into per-case unorderability, no-common-threshold incompatibility, and working-point gap (Fig.~\ref{fig:u03}). Representation (raw$\to$relational) collapses the first segment; flip coverage on relational input collapses the third; incompatibility is the largest segment in every arm.
The split replicates on the order-free D03-E bank ($n{=}1838$ quartets, fresh parents): ordering/incompatibility/working-point segments for raw+flip (0.122/0.648/0.016, 0.179/0.637/0.019, 0.154/0.636/0.053); rel+flip (0.024/0.322/0.051, 0.023/0.275/0.051, 0.020/0.281/0.050) --- same structure as dev512, so the decomposition is not bank-specific.

\paragraph{Coverage response (U07, supported on direction).} 25%-flip coverage on six-distance exceeds raw at 100% on both pools (6/6 seeds; Table~\ref{tab:u07}); on raw, more flip data helps but stays far below six at a quarter of the coverage. Coverage need is a function of structure, not of data volume.

\paragraph{Football geometry (D06, negative).} On 721 real WOY passes, paired keep+flip edits within the natural motion cap exist in 3.0% at event time (3.2% successful, 2.5% unsuccessful) and 3.3% 1.5\,s before; contested subpopulation (margin$<1$, n=278) 7.2%. Completed-pass geometry is open by selection; the quartet-bank design is infeasible there. The football anchor of the main text (zone crossing) is unaffected.
\paragraph{Fresh-bank confirmation (D09, confirmed).} On a new 236-quartet bank (unseen parents), six-distance beats raw by +0.259/+0.364/+0.195 (flip) and +0.106/+0.072/+0.178 (clean): 6/6 frozen predictions hit. Overlap audit: 18 quartets came from train\_101 parents; excluding them (n=218) Q1/Q2 still 6/6 (gaps +.26/+.37/+.22 flip, +.10/+.07/+.18 clean). A second fresh-parent bank (D03-E, $n{=}1838$, parents above the training range) reproduces the same four-arm ordering, making two independent fresh-bank confirmations.
\paragraph{Flip-loss weight (LAM, negative-for-cause).} $\lambda\in\{0.25,0.5,2.0\}$ gives J .042/.080/.089 / .068/.084/.059 / .080/.105/.063, flat within seed noise: $\lambda$ does not explain the large-scale flip-BCE collapses; g8 augmentation cures 6/6.
\paragraph{Vision resolution$\times$init factorial (D04).} ResNet-18 \citep{he2016deep} on rendered quartets, ImageNet-pretrained \citep{deng2009imagenet} versus random init, joint consistency $J$ (pretrained $|$ random), seeds s803/s805/s806: 64px: .353/.367/.272 $|$ .177/.174/.104; 96px: .517/.501/.547 $|$ .064/.431/.366; 128px: .676/.669/.602 $|$ .040/.563/.450; 224px: .720/.737/.709 $|$ .000/.662/.611; frozen-backbone linear head at 224px: .221/.225/.232. The pretrained prior is worth about $2\times$ at 64px but adds nothing at 224px, where random init matches it in 2/3 seeds---the 224px gain is resolution and readability, not the ImageNet prior. Random init collapses for s803 at every resolution ($J\le0.04$): a seed$\times$init basin effect, and full fine-tuning is required (linear head alone reaches only $.22$).
\paragraph{Relation supervision to an image student (U06, negative, robust at 224px).} ResNet18 student, same images/labels: endpoint-only (A), +generic-geometry aux (B), +relation aux (C). J: A .353/.367/.272, B .296/.229/.212, C .285/.358/.278; shuffled-target sanity 0.249. At 224px the ordering repeats (A .720/.737/.709; B .691/.506/.713; C .691/.735/.687; shuffled .708/.673/.686): C never exceeds A (one tie), and the shuffled-relation control is competitive, so no structured relation supervision transfers. The main claim stays coordinate-domain, and the vision line stops at the adapted-classifier result (D04).
\paragraph{Readout refit (U04, layer complementarity supported, narrowed).} Frozen-encoder refits (linear probes on frozen features \citep{kumar2022finetuning}) reproduce full-net sorting exactly (relflip static-readout S 0.8734/0.9198/0.8819); flip-readout gains appear only on the good encoder (relfeat +0.059--0.160); small-MLP adds <+0.021 everywhere (linear reachability); flip readout on raw encoders only migrates errors (R\_full .05--.06, M .39--.48).
\paragraph{Nearest-neighbor fair fight (D08, flipmine not special).} Same data/budget: PCT-style preserve matches flipmine (+0.008/-0.038/+0.000 on rel); balanced-half and random-half are within range on 2/3 and 1/3 seeds; temperature calibration moves nothing (24/24 cells). Method credit yields to diagnosis; U05 stays parked (regression gap <5pp gate unmet).
\paragraph{Decision frontier (D10, decision gain supported).} At matched coverage flip beats clean by median +0.236/+0.105/+0.085 (paired CIs mostly exclude zero); same holds at matched cost; monotone calibration replicates at most ~1/3 of the gain. Dev-matched coverage drifts on eval (reported per point); clean-best threshold degenerates.
\paragraph{Cross-task prediction (U10, principle transfer supported).} Frozen P-A/P-B/P-C all hit on point-in-triangle and segment-disk: six+flip beats raw+flip by +0.500/+0.563/+0.534/+0.392/+0.358/+0.356; six-25% beats raw-100% 6/6; task-adapted exact-invariance nets lose to sixdist 6/6 (and to raw once). Decomposition mirrors the source task; T2 raw+flip (J .61) shows it is not a hard-task artifact.
Orbit averaging replicates cross-task: it lifts flip-trained arms (T1 six +0.062/+0.041/+0.090; T2 raw +0.069/+0.069/+0.067), 12/12 flip cells positive per task, leaves clean arms flat, and is a null operation on exactly-invariant typed nets (all |delta| < .01, an internal protocol check).
\paragraph{Collapse attribution (D08-six).} A preserve-loss (pct) rerun on sixdist rescues the s47 collapse (J 0.376/0.439/0.452 vs flip-BCE .439/.426/.253): the collapse was loss-design, not seed fate; flipmine is again not special (pct mean .422 vs flipmine .373).
\paragraph{Decision frontier across encoders (D10-ext).} The matched-coverage decision gain replicates on stronger encoders: rel12 median +0.449/+0.199/+0.217; sixdist median +0.208/+0.118/+0.315; positive-pair fraction .95--1.0 everywhere. Decision gain is not raw-input specific.
\paragraph{Readout refit on the order-free bank (U04-E).} The scoped P2 pattern replicates on D03-E ($n{=}1838$): flip-readout helps static relfeat encoders (s11 +0.045, 3/3 positive) but not already-flip-trained ones; static-S matches D03 values within .002 (float-level borderline quartets).
